planting.note: Grow as a houseplant in medium to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; brighter light intensifies the neon-green leaf color.

directions: This Japanese-origin selection from the Terunoworld nursery resembles Neon Pothos at a glance, but its lime-green leaves develop odd raised crests or ridges on the underside that some growers describe as gill-like. Leaf color brightens noticeably with more light, though the vine still tolerates lower-light rooms without thriving there. In warm, humid conditions it sends out brown aerial roots along the stem that let it climb a pole or trellis past ten feet, or it can be left to trail from a basket or shelf.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant in bright, indirect natural light in well-drained potting mix; fading golden variegation signals a need for more light.

directions: Discovered in-house by Costa Farms plant hunter Mike Rimland and released as a patented exclusive, this vine carries dark green leaves rimmed in bold golden-yellow with occasional cream flecking, a bolder contrast than older gold-edged pothos selections. It is also the parent of the 'Lemon Top' sport, which emerges gold and fades to green as it matures, while 'Lemon Meringue' itself holds its gold edging on mature leaves given enough light. It climbs readily once mature, reaching six feet or more, and prefers the soil to dry about halfway down between waterings.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant in low to bright indirect light in well-drained potting mix; tolerates dim interior corners like other dracaenas in this group.

directions: This cultivar's strap-shaped leaves are a deep solid green edged in a narrow band of chartreuse, a subtler two-tone look than the broader white or cream stripes seen on Warneckii or White Jewel. It keeps the slow, upright cane habit typical of this dracaena group (sometimes sold under the older synonym Dracaena deremensis) and is commonly recommended for dimmer rooms where many flowering houseplants would struggle. Let the top half of the potting mix dry before watering again, and keep it away from cold drafts below about 55F.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant in low to bright indirect light in a fast-draining mix; let it dry out well between waterings like other hoyas.

directions: A trailing wax plant with rounded leaves, this species is grown as much for its delightfully fragrant red-and-white flower clusters as for its foliage. It shares the genus's tolerance for low, medium, or bright light and dislikes being watered before its chunky mix has dried out. Give it something to climb or let it cascade from a hanging basket, and expect blooming to be more reliable in brighter rooms than in dim ones.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant in medium to bright indirect light; let the top inch of mix dry before watering again to avoid root rot.

directions: This compact selection forms small, lance-shaped dark green leaves closely spaced along creeping stems, giving it a denser, finer texture than broader-leaved peperomias already in cultivation. Like most peperomias it tolerates low light but colors and fills in better in a medium or bright spot, and overwatering is the main threat to its shallow root system. It suits small pots, dish gardens, or mixed succulent-style arrangements where a low mounding texture is wanted.
